'''Francesco Giacomo Tricomi''' (5 May 1897 – 21 November 1978) was an Italian [[mathematician]] famous for his studies on mixed type [[partial differential equation]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Tricomi.html |title=Biography by J.J. O'Connor and E F Robertson |access-date=2008-10-18 |archive-date=2019-06-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605024930/http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Tricomi.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was also the author of a book on [[integral equation]]s.

==Biography==
[[File:Young Skewes Schieldrop Tricomi Cartwright Zurich1932.tif|thumb|Ms. Tricomi (3rd from right) accompanied Francesco Tricomi at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] 1932.]]
Tricomi was born in [[Naples]]. He first enrolled in the [[University of Bologna]], where he took chemistry courses. However, Tricomi realized that he preferred physics rather than chemistry; he moved to the University of Naples in 1915.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Francesco Tricomi - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Tricomi/ |access-date=2022-12-18 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref> He graduated at the [[University of Naples]] in 1918 and later was assistant to [[Francesco Severi]], first in [[Padua]] and then in [[Rome]]. Later he was professor at [[Turin]], called by [[Giuseppe Peano]], a position he held until his retirement in 1967.

He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1928 at Bologna<ref>{{cite book|author=Tricomi, F.|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1928.3/Main/icm1928.3.0027.0030.ocr.pdf|volume=3|chapter=Sull'equazione y ∂<sup>2</sup>z/∂x<sup>2</sup> + ∂<sup>2</sup>z/∂y<sup>2</sup> = 0.|title=''In:'' Atti del Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici: Bologna del 3 al 10 de settembre di 1928|pages=27–30|year=1929|access-date=2017-12-04|archive-date=2017-12-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171205093002/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1928.3/Main/icm1928.3.0027.0030.ocr.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 1932 in Zurich. From 1943 to 1945 and from  1948 to 1951 at the [[California Institute of Technology]] of  [[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]], he collaborated on the manual of special  functions for the [[Bateman Manuscript Project|Bateman manuscript project]], together with [[Arthur Erdélyi]], [[Wilhelm Magnus]] and Fritz Oberhettinger.

Tricomi was a member of the [[Accademia nazionale dei Lincei]] and of the ''Accademia delle Scienze di Torino'' (Turin Academy of Sciences), of which he was also president.
